clue.text: Cubs I help to make good investments

indicators.note: the letters are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Young scouts are encouraged to put their money into sound stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' tells you to rearrange the letters of CUBS I HELP.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares in large, reliable companies are called blue chips, after the highest-value poker counters.

clue.text: The attraction of misrule?

indicators.note: the prefix mis- means wrongly, so the word it is attached to is set out wrongly, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether lawlessness has its own appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits 'misrule' into 'mis' (wrongly) and 'rule': RULE arranged wrongly gives the answer. The question mark marks this unusual split.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is a bait or enticement, something that draws you in.

clue.text: Arab territory that makes me turn hot with resentment

indicators.note: to turn the little word round is to read its letters backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
irate means angry, hot with resentment

explanation.surface: A Gulf state that leaves the speaker flushed and angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses ME to EM, which is followed by IRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, such as those of the Arabian Gulf.

clue.text: Small vessel going over a stretch of water in Cheshire

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece goes over, above, the second

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel
a lake is a stretch of inland water

explanation.surface: A little boat crosses a lake somewhere in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoylake is a seaside town on the Wirral peninsula, historically in Cheshire, a county in north-west England; 'in Cheshire' defines it as a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition locates the town, a resort and golfing venue on the Wirral coast within that county.

clue.text: Piano song written for the theatre

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A piano number composed for a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a song for a musical, but 'song' gives LAY after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a work composed to be performed on stage.

clue.text: Became a person of discernment, eating caviare, for instance

definitions.meaning: to have come to appreciate refined things, gaining a palate for them
caviare is a classic food people learn to like only after trying it several times

explanation.surface: Someone grew sophisticated by learning to enjoy caviar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as a verb phrase, 'acquired' plus 'taste'; the second reads the answer as a noun phrase. 'eating' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses concern a liking developed over time, either the gaining of refined judgment or a food enjoyed only after getting used to it.

clue.text: Russia's most important political institution

parts.note: describes the highest legislative body of the old USSR, its words splitting into 'most important' and a Russian council

explanation.surface: A description of the top body in the Russian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most important' hints at the first word (highest), and the Russian word for a council gives the second.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the highest legislative assembly of the Soviet Union, the top council of the state.

clue.text: Very seldom does one come across anything that has it

definitions.text: Very seldom does one come across anything that has it

parts.words: Very seldom does one come across anything that has it
parts.note: describes the extra worth a thing gains purely because it is rare

explanation.surface: An observation that things with a certain quality are hard to find.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue states the economic idea in reverse: only rare things have this worth, so you rarely meet them.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists use this phrase for the premium an item commands because it is rare rather than useful.

clue.text: Abstemious member of biblical society?

parts.note: points to the Old Testament clan who refused wine, whose name was later taken by a temperance friendly society

explanation.surface: A question about a teetotaller in a scriptural group.
explanation.walkthrough: In Jeremiah 35 the descendants of Rechab refuse wine; the Independent Order of Rechabites was a British temperance friendly society named after them, so 'society' works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this biblical family abstained from wine, and the name passed to a nineteenth-century temperance order.

clue.text: Damaging statement of politician who has agreed to abstain from voting

definitions.text: statement of politician who has agreed to abstain from voting
definitions.meaning: an MP who 'pairs' with an opponent agrees that both will miss a vote

explanation.surface: A harmful remark from an MP who has agreed not to vote.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament, pairing is an arrangement where two MPs from opposing parties both stay away from a vote so their absences cancel out. Split the answer as I'M PAIRING to read the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Impairing means weakening or harming, and the same letters spoken as two words are what a paired MP would announce.

clue.text: Natives of Australia for whom air travel is out of the question

definitions.text: Natives of Australia for whom air travel is out of the question

parts.words: Natives of Australia for whom air travel is out of the question
parts.note: describes large Australian birds that cannot fly, dressed up as people who cannot take planes

explanation.surface: Australians who refuse to take flights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natives' suggests people, and 'air travel' suggests airliners; in fact these are flightless birds native to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: These large ratites are native to Australia and are flightless, so they never travel through the air.

clue.text: A revolutionary article brought into the market

indicators.note: one piece is brought into the other, placed inside it

parts.note: a mart is a market
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item of goods carried into a market by a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution, murdered in his bath. 'brought into' puts A inside MART.
explanation.definitionFit: Marat was a radical journalist and politician of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Stiffly formal cabinet-maker going round Rhode Island

indicators.note: the first piece goes round, enclosing, the second

parts.note: the Prime Minister, PM, chooses, makes, the cabinet
RI is the abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A stiff carpenter making furniture travels around a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabinet-maker' looks like a furniture builder but is the Prime Minister, who forms a cabinet; 'going round' puts PM around RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim describes a person who is stiffly proper and correct.

clue.text: Portugal's flow of capital

parts.note: a money phrase that really means the river flowing through Portugal's capital city, Lisbon

explanation.surface: A remark on money moving in and out of Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flow of capital' sounds financial, but it is a river flowing by the capital, Lisbon.
explanation.definitionFit: This river runs through Spain and Portugal and reaches the Atlantic at Lisbon.

clue.text: A bit of a fight?

explanation.surface: A question about part of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small fragment and a brief scuffle.

clue.text: A sack put in this position is naturally green

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other, placed inside it

parts.note: here means in this position
a bag is a sack

explanation.surface: A bag placed here turns out to be green by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places BAG inside HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is grass and leafy vegetation, which is green by nature.

clue.text: Laudations I came on haphazardly

indicators.note: done haphazardly, at random, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled on some words of praise by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haphazardly' rearranges I CAME ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomia, the plural of encomium, are formal speeches or writings of high praise.

clue.text: Not a street Arab who follows the herd

definitions.text: Not a street Arab who follows the herd

parts.words: Not a street Arab who follows the herd
parts.note: describes a desert-dwelling nomad who moves with his livestock, not a city urchin and not a conformist

explanation.surface: A city urchin who is not one to conform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'street Arab' was an old term for a homeless city child, and 'follows the herd' suggests conformity; literally this Arab lives in the desert and follows his animals.
explanation.definitionFit: These are nomadic Arabs of the desert who move with their camels, goats and sheep.

clue.text: Sort of thing that is put on at bedtime

definitions.text: Sort of thing that is put on at bedtime

parts.words: Sort of thing that is put on at bedtime
parts.note: describes a garment worn to sleep in, with 'that is' also hinting at the abbreviation i.e. and 'bedtime' at night

explanation.surface: A description of something done at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' sounds like a routine; it means a garment donned. 'bedtime' (NIGHT) and 'that is' (IE) also hint at the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is the garment many people wear in bed.

clue.text: No way to address a lady!

definitions.text: No way to address a lady!

parts.words: No way to address a lady!
parts.note: describes a letter opening suited only to a man, a salutation that would be wrong for a woman

explanation.surface: An indignant protest about speaking rudely to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way to address' sounds like a complaint about manners; it literally means a form of address used for men, not women.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal salutation for a letter to a man, so it cannot be used for a woman.

clue.text: Injured father figure lassoing wild game

indicators.note: to lasso is to catch with a loop, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: dad is a figure of a father

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hurt father ropes in some untamed animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges GAME to MAGE, and 'lassoing' puts that inside DAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaged means harmed, like a person who has been hurt.

clue.text: Essay about a literary dog

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, around, the second

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A written piece about a dog from literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' looks like a composition but means an attempt; 'about' puts TRY around A. Tray is a dog named by King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tray is one of the dogs King Lear names in Shakespeare's play, alongside Blanch and Sweetheart.

clue.text: South American trumpeter a U S soldier rings before noon

indicators.note: to ring is to encircle, so this piece encloses the next

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
AM means ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A trumpet player from South America surrounded by an American soldier in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trumpeter' suggests a musician, but the trumpeters are birds; 'rings' puts GI around AM.
explanation.definitionFit: The agami is a South American bird of the trumpeter family, named for its loud call.

clue.text: Heating chamber in which there are no vent-holes

indicators.note: the answer lies in the run of the following words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A hot room with no ventilation openings.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'nO VENt-holes'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is an enclosed compartment used for heating, baking or roasting.

clue.text: It helps to secure speed across water

definitions.meaning: a tie in rope that fastens things
a nautical mile per hour, the unit of a ship's speed

explanation.surface: A remark about tying up a fast boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and the second phrase run as one sentence, but there are two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fastening made in rope and a unit of speed at sea.

clue.text: A machine-gun nest put out of order

indicators.note: a jumbled order means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gun emplacement that has been knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out of order' rearranges NEST. A machine-gun nest is a gun position, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War.

clue.text: What allies should do is not to sit apart, apparently

definitions.text: What allies should do is not to sit apart, apparently

parts.words: What allies should do is not to sit apart, apparently
parts.note: plays on an idiom for unity, read literally as rising together rather than staying seated separately

explanation.surface: Advice that allies should not take separate seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' flags the literal reading: the opposite of sitting apart is rising to your feet at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to unite and support one another, as allies are expected to.

clue.text: Coming to a very sober conclusion

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Arriving at a completely sober finish.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, is a crossword favourite for a non-drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Attending means being present at, as in coming to a meeting.
